newsitem.title: GHANA: International consortium buys 40 pct of Ghana bank.
newsitem.headline: International consortium buys 40 pct of Ghana bank.

text.p: An international consortium of leading emerging market investment institutions has bought a 40 percent strategic stake in Ghana's Social Security Bank, the bank said in a statement.

The deal, in which the consortium paid $16.6 million for the stake, included a twinning agreement between the bank and Allied Irish Banks Plc (AIB) with the secondment of an AIB general operations manager, the statement added.
The sale concluded the privatisation of the bank, it said.

"Our involvement in this transaction signals our confidence in the long-term investment outlook for Ghana," the statement quoted Miles Morland, chief executive of London-based Blakeney Management, the consortium's lead investor, as saying.
"Last year's election has given the country a stable platform for Ghana," added Morland, whose company negotiated for the strategic stake.
Other consortium members include Morgan Stanley Asset Management, Alliance Capital Management, J P Morgan Investment Management and New Africa Investors.
The statement, dated Tuesday, said that these firms were among the first investors in Ghana following the opening of the Ghana Stock Exchange to foreign investors in 1993.
SSB was listed on the Stock Exchange in October 1995 when 21 percent of its stock was sold to the public at 800 cedis a share. Its price on Wednesday was 1,250 cedis.
SSB's 1996 after-tax profit was 26 billion cedis, a 60 percent increase over 1995's 16 billion cedis.

The statement said Dublin-based Allied Irish Banks, with assets of over $46 billion, had played a prominent role in providing management and technical services to banks in Central and Eastern Europe and in Asia.
It provides management services for a leading merchant bank in Nigeria and is also working with a bank group in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.
